title: I split an AI strategy game into model decisions, deterministic turns, and a Godot replay
author: ViceGodIm
selftext:
I built a mirrored island sim for ChatGPT and Claude. Each got structured state and chose one order every five game years. A separate world step resolved the two orders simultaneously; Godot replays the saved state, orders and messages. Claude helped me build the game.

The image shows the crossing after Claude’s first attack order. The useful debugging moment came later: Claude accused ChatGPT of crossing first, but the movement log at year 60 showed 31 Claude soldiers over the line and zero ChatGPT soldiers.

Here’s the single-run replay: [https://youtu.be/O2pj7vRlibU](https://youtu.be/O2pj7vRlibU)

What would you show in the UI so viewers can check an agent’s claim against the game state?
